counts_toward_budget: Yes. The model ran and produced work, and the rule forbidding such a round from being excused was written before this round started. The fault being the proctor's does not change that; budget.json cannot excuse it and is not being asked to.
error: Terminated mid-round by the proctor. The sandbox image rust:1.88-slim has no rustfmt component, so `cargo fmt` exited 1 with "'cargo-fmt' is not installed" for every input. Freezing requires fmt to exit 0, so no candidate in this image could ever have been freeze-ready: the round was unwinnable by construction. It was stopped rather than run to exhaustion because the feedback channel was carrying the model a compiler error it could not fix, which corrupts the measurement more than terminating does.

turns.refused: src/main.rs was emitted more than once. Two blocks for one path means the last one silently wins, and which one was meant is unknowable. Refused.

written_by: the proctor by hand, after killing round.py. round.py writes its own record at the end of a round and never got there, so this file is a reconstruction from the raw turn files in provenance/transcript/round-04/, which are the process's own output and were not edited. Digests here are computed from those files. Trust this record less than one round.py wrote.
